title: Getting in the Door: Streamlining Intake in Civil Legal Services with Large Language Models

model.params_source: paper Sec. 3.3 ('provided in a prompt to GPT-4-turbo with the temperature set to 0'); max_tokens and top_p assumed

task.subset_rule: all 48 scenario-jurisdiction pairs of dataset D1 (Table 1: 16 scenarios x 3 Missouri jurisdictions; 18 Accept, 25 Deny, 5 Question)
task.approximation: Only the initial response (experiment E1) is scored; the follow-up conversations of dataset D2 are a separate qualitative study. The 16 scenarios, the three jurisdictions' intake rules and the system prompt would all have to be recovered before a run.

items.source: dataset D1 is announced but not released: footnote 5 of the paper reads 'URL will be added to camera-ready paper'. The two repositories named in footnote 4 (github.com/lemmaLegalConsulting/docassemble-MOHUDEvictionProject and github.com/SuffolkLITLab/docassemble-ALToolbox) hold the application, not the evaluation data.
checks_2026_09_19: both repositories exist and are public (HTTP 200)

the jurisdiction intake rules in the app are a placeholder file: docassemble/MOHUDEvictionProject/data/sources/placeholder_intake_criteria.yml, header comment '# These are placeholder rules', with entries for seven Missouri programs; the paper's rule lengths (3,792 / 1,437 / 1,030 characters for Eastern, Mid- and Western Missouri) do not match it
no file in either repository holds the 16 scenarios or their Accept/Deny/Question labels

prompt.system: not printed in the paper; assembled at run time by docassemble.ALToolbox's IntakeQuestionList from an 'llm_role' instruction plus the jurisdiction's intake rules
prompt.user_template: not printed; Sec. 4.4.1 says the pipeline used the developed instructions as the system message and 'the intake rules from one of the jurisdictions together with one of the scenarios' as the user message
prompt.few_shot: none (Sec. 4.3: 'giving examples led to hallucinations, so the prompt omits example replies')
prompt.source_location: Sec. 4.3 and 4.4.1 describe the prompt; the text itself is only in the GitHub repositories
prompt.verbatim: none: the paper prints no prompt text, and the current ALToolbox code builds the prompt at run time with 2026 defaults (the interview file asks for model gpt-5.2), so the 2024 wording used for the paper is not the wording a reader gets today

output.postprocess: strip, lowercase; the paper captured the prediction plus a narrative explanation

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: weighted-average F1 over the three classes Accept / Deny / Question, weighted by class proportion; the runner implements macro_f1 and micro_f1 but not the proportion-weighted variant, so a hook score() would be needed
metric.original_location: Table 3, row GPT-4-turbo, column Weighted average F1 (P 0.86, R 0.81, F1 0.82). The triage record points at Table 4, which is the same model broken down by jurisdiction (0.94 / 0.69 / 0.84).

open_points: Dataset D1 (48 scenario-jurisdiction pairs with Accept/Deny/Question labels) is not published: the paper's footnote 5 promises a camera-ready URL and neither linked repository contains it.
The prompt is not printed anywhere in the paper; the repository builds it at run time and its current version targets a 2026 model, so the 2024 wording cannot be recovered from the public record.
The jurisdiction intake rules that go into the prompt are a placeholder file in the public repository and do not match the character counts given in Sec. 3.2.
Metric gap: weighted-average F1 is not one of the runner's metric names.
notes: GPT-4-turbo is the best of the eight models tested and was also the model on which the prompt was iteratively refined, which the authors name as a limitation (Sec. 6). A reproduction would have to reconstruct three artefacts at once (scenarios, labels, prompt), so no run configuration can be made binding.
